15c_1_transition_orbitals.png: Left: the orbitals (components $a$ solid, $b$ dashed; vertical axis, normalised) of the occupied fold-band level (blue) and the empty bulk level (orange) of the sector $n_2 = 10$, $j = +1$, even fold condition, of the free state $N = 592$ at $a_{4,0} = 0$, against $y$ (horizontal axis). Right: the integrand of their matrix element $\langle n|\partial_a h|m\rangle$ (units of $m$), its momentum part and its kinetic part from the shrinking hidden direction; the size of the area under the sum is $0.1031\,m$, and with the energy difference $0.8592\,m$ it gives $Q = 0.1397$, the largest of this state.
15c_2_q_by_pair.png: The adiabaticity measure $Q_{nm}$ (vertical axis, logarithmic, pure number) of every allowed transition of the free states $N = 8$ (triangles), $N = 592$ (circles) and $N = 2352$ (open squares) at $a_{4,0} = 0$, against the shell $n_2$ of the sector (horizontal axis); colour: the label of the empty level. The jumps to label 1 dominate and grow with the momentum; even the zero modes at $k = 0$ can jump, through the kinetic term of the shrinking hidden direction. All values lie below $0.2$ (the largest is $0.1943$).
15c_3_q_history.png: Left: the largest adiabaticity measure $Q_{max}$ (vertical axis, logarithmic) of the 75 ground states, $N = 8$ (dotted), $N = 592$ (solid) and $N = 2352$ (dashed), for the five couplings (colours; the legend names them for $N = 592$), against the slice (horizontal axis), from the record; black crosses: the values recomputed here for $\lambda = 0$. Right: the transition probability estimate $Q_{max}^2$, below $0.039$ everywhere. Both fall along the history.
15c_4_hellmann_feynman.png: The derivative $d\varepsilon/da_4$ (vertical axis, units of $m$) of the occupied fold-band levels (blue) and of the first bulk level of each of their sectors (orange) of the free state $N = 2352$ at $a_{4,0} = 1$, against the momentum $k$ of the shell (horizontal axis): circles from Richardson finite differences of the levels, crosses from the matrix element of $\partial_a h$. They agree (the Hellmann-Feynman theorem). The fold band falls like $-\kappa k$; the bulk levels rise at small $k$, because the hidden direction shrinks, and fall at large $k$, where the momentum term wins.
15c_5_fermi_crossing.png: The Fermi-level crossing of the demonstration state $N = 2360$ without interaction. Left: the fold-band level of the shell $n_2 = 27$ (blue) falls along the history and the odd bulk level at $k = 0$ (orange) rises; they cross almost at once, at $a_{4,0} = 0.0047$ (dotted line), because at $a_{4,0} = 0$ the band lies only $0.0067\,m$ above the bulk level; vertical axis in units of $m$. Right: the energy by which the adiabatically continued state lies above the instantaneous aufbau state (vertical axis, units of $m$), from the record (dots) and from the two levels (crosses), at the five slices.
15c_6_q_map.png: Heat map of the largest adiabaticity measure $Q_{max}$ of the 75 ground states of the canonical matrix (record): rows are the particle numbers $N = 8$, $592$, $2352$ with the couplings $0$, $\pm\lambda_1$, $\pm\lambda_2$ (tags lam0, lamp1, lamm1, lamp2, lamm2), columns the slices $a_{4,0}$; the printed numbers are the values. Every value is below $0.2$, the largest at the start of the history and for the largest particle number.
